why: The O2 replacement made the scorer prefer the later cut that preserves a fronted adjunct, so cuts were pushed later and the top-of-list choices at shallow depths shifted into deeper ranks. That produced gains for short-latency bins (≤3–7 pieces) which keep many candidates (rank-depth coincidence improved at deeper depths) but slightly reduced top-1 precision and produced a small loss for the longest bin (≤99).
lesson: When preferring later cuts to keep fronted adjuncts intact, retain or recover precision for the very top ranks so long-latency budgets (which rely on the first one or two positions) are not harmed.
